questions_and_answers.question_text: What does the syllable yóu mean?
How many syllables does náqu have, and what does it not specify?
What does reduplication of zhǎo indicate?
What does kàn mean after a reduplicated verb?
Write the Chinese for "Give it a try and see."
Write the Chinese for "Go ask him and see."
Which directional ending is used only with -lái?
Write the Chinese for "Let's hear what it is."

articles.text:
2. A: Wǒ xiǎng kànkan jīntian yǒu    I'd like to see what ads there are
      shénme guǎnggào.               today.
   B: Zhèr yǒu yífèn Huáshèngdùn    Here's a copy of the Washington Post,
      Yóubào, náqu zhǎozhǎo kàn ba!  take it and try to find some.

Notes on No. 2

Yóubào: "Post," in the name of a newspaper. The syllable yóu means "post" or "mail," as in yóujú, "post office." (Names of other newspapers use the same pattern: Shíbào is "Times," Rìbào is "Daily," Kuàibào is "Express.")

náqu...: "take away." This is a compound verb of DIRECTION. Many compound verbs you have seen have THREE syllables. But náqu has only TWO: the main action verb and the relative motion (away). The DIRECTION of the action (up, down, in, out) is NOT specified.

Main Verb | Direction        | Relative Motion (Towards or Away)
ná        | chū              | lái
zǒu       | jìn              | qù
pǎo       | xià              |
kāi       | shàng            |
bān       | guò              |
          | qǐ- (only with -lái)

zhǎozhǎo kàn: "try to find." Zhǎo is REDUPLICATED here, meaning the action lasts an indefinite amount of time: "look a little bit." KÀN following a reduplicated verb means "AND SEE (if it works, if it's okay, if you can do it)."

Nǐ shìshi kàn ba.                Give it a try and see.
Nǐ zuòzuo kàn, zhèige shāfā      Sit down and try it out. This sofa
zhēn shūfu.                      is really comfortable.
Bù zhīdào, nǐ qù wènwen kàn.     I don't know. Go ask him and see.
Nǐ shuōshuo kàn.                 Let's hear what it is.
